In Altamont, West Vancouver, the 55+ homes you can buy are Nearest, outside the sub-area and Nearest, outside the sub-area (strata). The other seniors housing here, which you cannot buy into, is rental and retirement residence or care. This page names each building, says what type it is and what the sources show, and covers local rules and the questions buyers ask. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.
55+ strata buildings you can buy in Altamont
Nearest, outside the sub-area — Westview Terrace, 1390 Duchess Avenue (Ambleside)

A North Shore realty guide lists it among West Vancouver buildings that "all have a 55+ bylaw," and a current listing for the building describes "a quiet, well-kept 25-unit concrete building (55+)" in the heart of Ambleside, two blocks to the village, seawall and beach. Treat the bylaw as listing/guide-stated and confirm it in the strata documents before relying on it.
Nearest, outside the sub-area — Tudor Gardens, 843 22nd Street (Dundarave)

Built 1992. Building sources record age restrictions, pets not allowed and rentals not allowed, and a listing for the building states the rule plainly: "55+ age restriction, no pets," with a large activity room, library and courtyard, one block from the seawall and across from the West Vancouver Community Centre. The "rentals not allowed" line in older building data cannot stand as a long-term rental ban under current BC law — — so confirm the building's current position from its bylaws and Form B.
Rental, care and subsidized seniors housing in Altamont (not for sale)

items.t: Nearest, outside the sub-area — the Kiwanis cluster on 21st Street / Gordon Avenue (Ambleside): Kiwanis North Shore Housing Society provides independent living apartments at below-market rates for adults 55+ on the North Shore. Its West Vancouver buildings are Kiwanis Manor, 959 21st Street (the society's own page labels it "55+ • WEST VANCOUVER," independent living, applications year-round, North Shore residents given preference, no pets), The Court, 2151 Gordon Avenue, The Cypress, 999 21st Street, and The Terrace, 975 21st Street. Society-wide eligibility in its application material: capable of living independently, non-smoker, 55 or older, with income and asset limits that are updated annually against BC Housing's low-and-moderate income limits. Rental only — nothing to buy.

Amica West Vancouver — 659 Clyde Avenue: Registered assisted living, operator Amica West Vancouver Inc.; Amica describes private independent-living and assisted-living suites plus licensed residential care at this address.

Amica Lions Gate — Keith Road: Registered assisted living, class SN. The Registry's crawled listings give the address two ways — 727 Keith Road and 701-721 Keith Road — while the operator's own page gives 701-727 Keith Road; use the operator's range and treat the exact civic range as a minor source conflict. Amica states it offers independent living, assisted living, long-term care, memory care and respite at this residence.

Hollyburn House — 2095 Marine Drive: Registered assisted living, class SN, now marketed by Cogir as Venvi Hollyburn House; the operator lists independent living, assisted living, residential care, short-term and respite stays, across from the Seniors' Activity Centre and library, between Ambleside and Dundarave.

Inglewood Care Centre — 725 Inglewood Avenue (Ambleside side): Long-term care, not a purchase: opened 1979, operated by Baptist Housing Society (not for profit), 230 publicly funded beds as of March 31, 2025, all single/double occupancy per the BC Seniors Advocate's facility file. Access is through Vancouver Coastal Health assessment, not by buying or applying to the building as housing.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Altamont

items.t: Altamont is a residential hillside area of the District of West Vancouver, above Marine Drive between Dundarave to the east and Caulfeild to the west. The District does not use "Altamont" as a named neighbourhood in its Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 4985, 2018 — its village centres are Dundarave, Caulfeild Village and Horseshoe Bay, with Ambleside as the Municipal Town Centre — so street-by-street boundaries for Altamont are UNVERIFIED.

The streets that frame the area are Marine Drive along the waterfront below, Queens Avenue climbing the hillside, and the avenues above them below the British Properties edge; nearby areas are Dundarave (east), Caulfeild (west), the British Properties (north, uphill), Ambleside (south-east) and Chelsea Park (north-west, uphill).

Housing form: detached houses on hillside lots in the RS single-family zones of Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010. No condo building, townhome complex or seniors facility inside Altamont is confirmed on an official or developer source —.

Transit at the edges, not inside: TransLink route 251 (Queens / Park Royal), operated as West Vancouver Blue Bus, runs on the Queens Avenue corridor below the hillside, and route 250 runs on Marine Drive between Horseshoe Bay, Dundarave, Park Royal and downtown Vancouver via the Lions Gate Bridge.

Schools: School District 45 (West Vancouver Schools) catchments are address-based and no Altamont catchment is confirmed — SD45 directs families to the school locator on its admissions page. SD45 has no middle tier: elementary is K–7, secondary is 8–12. Nearby schools are Irwin Park Elementary (K–7), 2455 Haywood Avenue in Dundarave, and Westcot Elementary (K–7) at the foot of the British Properties.

Health care: Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver, is the Vancouver Coastal Health hospital serving the North Shore including West Vancouver; the North Vancouver Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at Suite 200, 221 West Esplanade, North Vancouver.

The District's seniors hub is downhill in Ambleside: the West Vancouver Seniors' Activity Centre, 695 21st Street, offers programs, services and amenities geared toward 55+ adults, including the Garden Side Bistro, fitness, arts and learning programs and a seniors' shuttle bus. It is a program centre, not housing.

blocks.text: Local rules and plans in Altamont

items.t: District zoning: Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010: Altamont houses sit in the RS single-family zones; Section 200 states minimum site areas of 8,094 m² in RS1, 1,625 m² in RS2, 975 m² in RS3, 731 m² in RS4 and 488 m² in RS5, and lists secondary suites and a detached secondary suite (coach house) among permitted uses. The bylaw's ground-oriented rules allow 4 dwellings per lot, or 6 if the site is wholly or partly within 400 metres of a prescribed bus stop — the legal route to staying in the area with a suite or coach house rather than moving to a 55+ building.

Density rules on the lower streets are in transition: On July 21, 2025, the Province directed West Vancouver to amend its OCP to provide increased density in the single-family and duplex areas adjacent to Ambleside and Dundarave (and at Park Royal–Taylor Way) by December 31, 2025 — Altamont sits directly above Dundarave, so verify infill rules per property. On December 1, 2025, Council adopted OCP Amendment Bylaw No. 5406, 2025, bringing the OCP into alignment with the 2024 Interim Housing Needs Report.

OCP context on seniors housing: the District's own Canada Community-Building Fund reporting states West Vancouver's population has aged faster than the region's — seniors were about one in five residents in 2001 and nearly one in three in 2021, with a median age of 51 in 2021 — and the 2018 OCP's housing theme expressly aims to provide "more and ongoing seniors and rental housing options," while noting seniors are among those unable to find accessible, single-level options close to amenities and transit. That is the policy backdrop: demand is documented, supply inside pockets like Altamont is not.

Hazard permits on hillside lots: an Environmental Development Permit is required for work within 15 metres of the top of any watercourse bank, and a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit for work within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface; a Foreshore Development Permit applies to waterfront/coastal-flood-risk property below the hillside.

Taxes: District of West Vancouver 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid current taxes on July 2, 2026 and a further 5% on outstanding current taxes on September 2, 2026. At Altamont price points the Province's additional school tax can also apply — 0.2% on the residential portion of assessed value between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027. Water and sewer are metered and billed quarterly.

blocks.text: The BC rules on 55+ age bylaws, who may own and who may live in a unit, the exemptions and rentals apply in every strata and are explained once, with sources, on the BC 55+ strata rules page.

items.t: BC 55+ strata rules

The whole District has only three buildings a North Shore guide lists as 55+-bylaw strata — Westview Terrace (1390 Duchess Ave), Tudor Gardens (843 22nd St) and Lincoln Gardens (whose address the guide page does not state — UNCONFIRMED here). A buyer searching "Altamont 55+" is really searching Ambleside and Dundarave; the hillside pockets contribute no supply at all.

The demand side is documented by the District itself: seniors rose from about one in five West Vancouver residents in 2001 to nearly one in three in 2021, and the median age hit 51 in 2021 — a decade older than the regional median — yet the OCP still describes the District as mostly detached, single-family housing with limited other forms.

The biggest seniors project in the District's history is the Inglewood redevelopment, and it is not in Altamont. On September 21, 2026, Council approved bylaws and a development permit to redevelop Inglewood Care Centre at 725 Inglewood Ave in two phases: Phase 1, a 364-bed publicly funded long-term care facility; Phase 2, 200 independent-living units and 161 seniors rental housing units. The District is not involved in tenant placement — Baptist Housing handles resident inquiries.

"Age restrictions" on a building-data site is not the same as verified 55+. Wedgewood Terrace (1730 Duchess Ave) is recorded with age restrictions but no stated threshold in the sources checked; since Nov 24, 2022 any BC strata age bylaw below 55 is invalid anyway, so the registered bylaw — not the database line — is what decides who can live there.

Kiwanis Manor carries two different descriptions in two official-ish sources — independent 55+ rental on the operator society's site, registered assisted living in BC's Assisted Living Registry under a partnership name. Anyone referring a client there should confirm which product the building actually offers before describing it.

The seawalk below the hillside is the flat walking route: the Centennial Seawalk runs roughly 1.7 km east from Dundarave Park (150 25th Street, with 50+ metres of sandy beach, playground, washrooms and a seasonal concession) to Ambleside — relevant to any senior buyer weighing a hillside house against a flat Ambleside condo.

The District runs a dedicated 55+ service layer downhill: the Seniors' Activity Centre at 695 21st Street runs the Garden Side Bistro, the SACS on 21st shop, rehabilitation/fitness programs and a seniors' shuttle bus — services an Altamont senior uses by driving or bussing down to Ambleside, not services in the pocket.

faq.q: What 55+ homes can I actually buy in Altamont?
faq.a: None inside the pocket — no verified 55+ strata (or any strata) exists in Altamont in any source checked; the housing is detached freehold houses. The nearest verified 55+ ownership buildings are downhill in Ambleside and Dundarave: Westview Terrace, 1390 Duchess Ave, and Tudor Gardens, 843 22nd St.

faq.q: Is there a 55+ rental building near Altamont?
faq.a: Yes, in Ambleside: the Kiwanis North Shore Housing Society's West Vancouver buildings (Kiwanis Manor, 959 21st St; The Court, 2151 Gordon Ave; The Cypress, 999 21st St; The Terrace, 975 21st St) are independent-living rentals for 55+, below-market, with income/asset eligibility and preference for North Shore residents. Rental only — nothing to buy, and pets are not permitted in Kiwanis seniors communities.

faq.q: Building data says Tudor Gardens has "rentals not allowed." Is that still true?
faq.a: Not as a long-term rental ban — every strata rental-restriction bylaw in BC became invalid on Nov 24, 2022. The tenant must still satisfy the 55+ bylaw or an exemption, and short-term rentals can still be restricted. Confirm the building's current bylaws and Form B rather than relying on older building-data lines.

faq.q: Are pets allowed in the nearest 55+ options?
faq.a: It splits by building: Tudor Gardens is recorded as no pets, and Kiwanis seniors communities do not permit pets; Westview Terrace's pet position is UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked — confirm in the bylaws/Form B for the specific building.

faq.q: If I stay in my Altamont house, can I add a suite or coach house instead of moving?
faq.a: That is the route the zoning contemplates: secondary suites and detached secondary suites are permitted uses in the RS single-family zones, and the ground-oriented rules allow up to 4 dwellings per lot (6 within 400 m of a prescribed bus stop), subject to the lot's zone and permits — including the wildfire-interface and watercourse development permits that apply on this hillside.

Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver — the Vancouver Coastal Health hospital serving the North Shore, including West Vancouver. The North Vancouver Urgent and Primary Care Centre (Suite 200, 221 West Esplanade) is the urgent-care option.

faq.q: If I need care later, can I stay in West Vancouver?
faq.a: The in-District ladder is: registered assisted-living residences at Amica West Vancouver (659 Clyde Ave), Amica Lions Gate (Keith Rd) and Hollyburn House (2095 Marine Dr), then long-term care at Inglewood Care Centre (725 Inglewood Ave, 230 publicly funded beds). All are in the Ambleside/Park Royal side of the District, downhill from Altamont — none is in the pocket itself.

faq.q: What transit can I actually use day to day from Altamont?
faq.a: The confirmed service is at the edges: route 251 on Queens Avenue and route 250 on Marine Drive, both West Vancouver Blue Bus routes to Park Royal. Most Altamont streets are a hill walk or a drive from those corridors, and the Seniors' Activity Centre runs its own shuttle bus for 55+ members downhill in Ambleside.
